lecture_beats.subject: Rotations act on vectors, vector fields, rigid objects, and quantum states.
Successive rotations compose to another rotation and motivate the group structure.
Axis-angle parameterization, right-hand convention, opposite axes, and periodicity caveat.
A unit axis needs two angles and the rotation angle supplies a third parameter.
Closure, identity, inverse, and associativity of rotations.
Noncommutativity, order of x and y rotations, and the small-angle qualification.
Audience clarification that group multiplication means sequential rotations.
The destination is the three-state red-green-blue color symmetry of quarks.
Vector components and the three-dimensional matrix representation.
Active rotation of a vector versus rotation of coordinate axes.
The axis-angle-dependent matrix law V prime equals R V.
Invariant length as the defining physical requirement for a real rotation matrix.
Dummy-index derivation of R_ij R_ik equals delta_jk.
Transpose notation, R transpose R equals one, and inverse equals transpose.
Matrix multiplication reproduces group multiplication; representations need not be unique.
Spin-one states form a three-component vector representation and motivate vector particles.
Discrete versus continuous groups, phase and rotation examples, and Lie-group terminology.
Spin zero carries the trivial one-dimensional representation.
Spin-up and spin-down basis columns and a general two-component spinor.
Normalization, chosen z axis, and generic spin-polarization direction.
Physical or coordinate rotation of a spinor by a two-by-two matrix.
The deferred two-valuedness subtlety of the spinor representation.
Probability preservation for complex spinor amplitudes and parameter counting of a pure state.
Hermitian conjugation and the unitary condition U dagger U equals one.
Eight real matrix components minus four unitarity constraints leaves four.
A spatial rotation has three parameters, so one further restriction is required.
Determinant one is compatible with products, identity, and a closed subgroup.
The three-parameter special-unitary action on spin-one-half states and its caveat.
Audience exchange on determinant phases of U and U dagger.
Definitions of U(n), U(1), SU(n), and SU(2).
Audience question locating the spin and Pauli matrices in the construction.
Group elements close to identity describe infinitesimal rotations.
First-order unitarity makes the unmodified generator anti-Hermitian.
Extracting i converts the infinitesimal generator to a Hermitian matrix.
First-order determinant expansion gives the trace and imposes tracelessness.
Traceless Hermitian two-by-two matrices are linear combinations of Pauli matrices.
The rotation axis selects the corresponding Pauli-matrix linear combination.
Combining representations is deferred in favor of returning to quarks.
Color is a three-state degree of freedom represented by amplitudes or three field operators.
Discrete color exchanges sit inside a larger continuous group; determinant phase correction.
Special-unitary three-by-three matrices act on the color triplet.
Physics is invariant under the internal SU(3) color mixing, distinct from spatial rotation.
Eighteen real parameters minus nine unitarity conditions and determinant one leaves eight.
The same eight underlies the eight gluons; determinant language is heuristic.
SU(3) is the basic QCD symmetry and constrains every allowed Lagrangian term.
The QCD construction is deferred after establishing the symmetry framework.
